method: Reverse-DCF: solve for the constant annual FCF growth the current price implies. 10-yr explicit FCF + Gordon terminal; discount 10%, terminal growth 2.5%. value(g)=sum_i fcf*(1+g)^i/(1.10)^i + [fcf*(1+g)^10*1.025/0.075]/(1.10)^10; implied g solved (bisection) so (value+netcash)/shares = price. FCF/shares/net-cash are real TTM figures (Q1 2026). Higher implied g = more growth already priced in.

names.note: Undemanding: price implies only ~6.5%/yr FCF growth for a decade. Supports the value read; handset/licensing cyclicality is the main risk to even that bar.
